scenes.headline: How one image generator learned to draw depth
scenes.sub: A picture and its depth map, denoised in one sequence
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Perpetua! Today, an image generator that also draws how far away everything is.

scenes.text: Depth is encoded as an image by the same autoencoder and placed in the same token sequence, so one transformer denoises picture and depth together.
scenes.say: The trick: turn depth into a picture, and put it in the same sequence as the image. One transformer denoises both.

scenes.title: Depth, written as an image
scenes.say: First, depth must look like an image.

parts.note: log of the distance along each pixel's ray
parts.say: Take the log of each pixel's distance.

parts.note: set per image from its own percentiles
parts.say: Squeeze every image's range into the same band.

parts.note: unknown at test time, so depth is relative
parts.say: That scale and shift are unknown later, so the depth is relative, and benchmarks must align it first.

steps.say: A prompt, an image, and a depth map. Image and depth share one autoencoder.
Their tokens join one sequence. An image token and its depth token share a position.
One transformer denoises it all. The only new weights are a tiny table saying which token is which.
Out comes a picture with its depth. No depth head, no second network.

scenes.title: Four tasks, same weights
scenes.say: Only what starts as noise changes.

items.say: Both noisy: a picture with its depth.
Photo given clean: only depth is denoised.
Depth given clean: paint a picture onto it.
Depth left as noise: a plain image generator.
